steps.intent: Enter the operator ID to sign on

strategies.rationale: The textbox named "Operator ID" — how an operator identifies it, so it survives restyling and relayout and breaks only if the label itself changes.
The textbox whose label cell reads "Operator ID". Independent of the accessible name, so it still resolves if the label is reworded.

Form field name "operator". In a server-rendered application this is part of the HTTP contract, so changing it means changing the request handler. Ranked below semantic strategies because it is invisible to users, so a rewrite can rename it without anyone noticing.

Generated control id "ctl00_txtOperator". Ids of this shape encode the server control tree, so they change whenever the page is restructured and are usually the first locator to break after a vendor upgrade. Kept for debugging and tie-breaking, not for driving.

steps.intent: Capture the savings account balance requested by the goal

target.description: the "Balance" value in the row containing "Savings"

strategies.rationale: The cell under the "Balance" column in the row containing "Savings". A value in a data grid needs both coordinates: cells in one row share the same neighbours, so a row label alone matches several of them. Matching the column by header text rather than position also survives columns being reordered.
The text next to "Savings". Ranked below the grid coordinate, which also pins the column. 2 elements on the recorded screen match this, so on its own it cannot tell them apart.

successCheckpoint.description: The screen shows a grid with a "Balance" column, where the returned value is read from.

knownOutcomes.description: The application rejected the supplied operator credentials. A legitimate answer, not a fault: retrying cannot help, and neither can a person taking over the session, because the credential the caller holds is the one that is wrong. Without this outcome the run goes on to look for the next screen's controls, fails as target_not_found, and — with escalation enabled — pages an operator over a wrong password.
No member exists with the supplied ID. A legitimate answer, not a failure.
The member record exists but this operator's role cannot view it. The caller needs to distinguish this from not-found, because the remedy is an access request rather than a corrected ID.
The application rejected the member ID's format. The caller supplied a malformed value.
The application rejected the submitted values. The caller should correct inputs and retry.
The application reported that a required field was not supplied.

detector.pattern: \b(Operator ID|Password|Member ID|Account Type|Initial Deposit) is required\b

knownOutcomes.description: The member has no open accounts at all, so there is no savings balance to return.
The member's accounts are showing, but none of them is a savings account, so there is no savings balance to return.

provenance.goal: Sign on with operator ID '{operatorId}' and password '[REDACTED]', then look up member {memberId} and read their current savings balance.

revisions.summary: Replay review found two legitimate answers reported as failures. A member whose only account is checking, and a closed member with no accounts, both ran out the full step timeout and failed with target_not_found, which with escalation enabled would page a person. Neither is a fault: there is simply no savings balance to return, and the caller needs to know which case applies.
